metadata.title: Macro Delete Path Traversal via Unvalidated selectedMacro

sources: sessionStorage macroFileList (populated from ApplinX REST API, persisted across logout)
transformations: getMacroListDetails() reads macroFileList, splits on comma — no per-item validation
selected($event) stores event + '.json' into this.selectedMacro — no MACRO_NAME_PATTERN validation
sinks: MacroService.deleteMacro(macroName, user, app, token) → ApplinX REST API DELETE endpoint
URL path construction in @ibm/applinx-rest-apis SDK (URL encoding behavior unknown)

privilege_boundary.start_privilege: Authenticated ApplinX user with macro permissions (or XSS executor via VULN-004)
privilege_boundary.achieved_privilege: Arbitrary file deletion/read on ApplinX server filesystem (if server unprotected)

impact.description: Arbitrary file read or deletion on ApplinX server filesystem via path traversal in macro name. Impact conditioned on: (1) ApplinX SDK not URL-encoding path params, (2) ApplinX server not validating macro names server-side. Attack chain: VULN-004 XSS → VULN-009 sessionStorage injection → VULN-007 delete.

prerequisites: Prior XSS (VULN-004) OR physical/malware access to browser console to inject sessionStorage
ApplinX REST API server not validating macro name server-side
ApplinX SDK not URL-encoding path parameters

compensating_controls: ApplinX SDK may URL-encode path params (unverified — if true, client-side fix sufficient)

remediation.fix_approach: Apply MACRO_NAME_PATTERN validation (/^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$/) in MacroComponent.selected() before storing selectedMacro. Filter macroList on load. Fix modal state inconsistency: onDeleteMacro() should use selectedDelMacro. Clear macroFileList in StorageService.setNotConnected() (companion VULN-009 fix).

history.note: onDeleteMacro() passes selectedMacro directly to ApplinX REST API without MACRO_NAME_PATTERN validation

Confirmed path traversal via sessionStorage injection. Requires prior XSS (VULN-004) or VULN-009 as prerequisite. CVSS HIGH 8.0 reflecting server filesystem impact (conditioned on SDK/server behavior). Part of AC-003 attack chain.
